trials.name: BioFINDER-1
trials.population: Mild cognitive impairment and cognitively healthy elderly subjects
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to conversion to clinically probable AD in subjects with normal vs abnormal biomarkers
trials.results_summary: The cohort established foundational evidence on the temporal evolution of Alzheimer's biomarkers, validating the utility of CSF/plasma markers and PET imaging to predict cognitive decline in predementia populations.

trials.name: BioFINDER-2
trials.population: Cognitively healthy individuals, SCD/MCI, AD dementia, and other dementias
trials.primary_endpoint: Clinical diagnosis and Change in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB)
trials.results_summary: Ongoing prospective cohort. Baseline and early longitudinal data from this cohort were used in the reported document to simulate and validate the two-step screening approach for future preclinical AD trials.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3
trials.population: Cognitively unimpaired participants with preclinical Alzheimer's disease (intact cognition but P-tau results consistent with amyloid pathology)
trials.primary_endpoint: Time to Clinical Progression of Composite Endpoint as Measured by Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR)

trials.name: AHEAD 3-45
trials.population: Cognitively unimpaired individuals with Preclinical and Early Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease (elevated or intermediate amyloid)
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) Score

related_evidence.description: Baseline data publication from TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3 demonstrating the real-world implementation of p-tau screening in a Phase 3 preclinical AD trial.
Prospective cohort study from the BioFINDER group evaluating plasma tau biomarkers for Alzheimer's diagnosis and stratification.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting the use of plasma p-tau217 and tau-PET for prognostic enrichment in Alzheimer's disease trials is robust and is actively shaping current Phase 3 designs. The BioFINDER 1 and 2 observational cohorts have repeatedly validated the predictive accuracy of these biomarkers for cognitive decline, particularly using composite endpoints like mPACC5. This two-step sequential screening hypothesis forms the foundation of modern preclinical interventional trials aimed at reducing screen failure rates and sample sizes. For instance, the fully enrolled TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3 trial of donanemab explicitly utilizes blood p-tau screening to identify cognitively unimpaired individuals with underlying amyloid pathology. Similarly, the AHEAD 3-45 trial of lecanemab targets asymptomatic individuals with biomarker-confirmed pathology and evaluates decline using the PACC5 endpoint, directly mirroring the document's simulated outcome measures. While the document presents this screening method as a simulation, major ongoing clinical programs have already heavily integrated these blood-based biomarker prescreening strategies into their protocols.
discrepancies: The document presents the two-step screening approach (blood p-tau followed by advanced imaging) as a simulation for future trial optimization, but registry records show this paradigm is already actively utilized in major ongoing Phase 3 preclinical AD trials (e.g., TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3).
